clue.text: Court after blunder not having good influence

indicators.note: 'not having' tells us a letter standing for a word in the clue is taken away

blocks.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
G is the usual abbreviation for good; it is removed
CT is the abbreviation for court, as in street names

explanation.surface: A tennis player's mistake on court costs them their good sway over the match.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFE loses its G to leave AFFE, and the court abbreviation follows it, since 'after' puts it second.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect something is to have an effect on it, so the verb is a straight synonym for influence.

clue.text: Cat shown by artist under tropical tree, miles away

indicators.note: 'miles away' asks for the letter standing for miles to be sent off from the tree
in a down clue being under means sitting lower, so the artist is sent second, after the tree

blocks.note: the mango tree grows in the tropics
M is the abbreviation for miles; it is removed
RA, Royal Academician, is crossword shorthand for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's picture shows a cat beneath a mango tree far from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts the artist below, that is after, the shortened tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a long-haired breed of domestic cat, so the breed name serves as an example of the definition.

clue.text: Worrier in place supporting loud American

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means holding up from below, so the place is sent second

blocks.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
US is the standard short form for American
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: A worried person finds themselves stuck next to a loud American.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means sitting underneath, so the place comes after the loud American.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot frets over trivial things, making the informal noun a fair description of a habitual worrier.

clue.text: Trick involving meat and eel confused with lizard

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up, so the letters of the fish name are jumbled
to involve is to wrap up within, so the trick goes around the rest

blocks.note: a con is a trick or swindle
ham is a kind of meat
the fish's letters, jumbled

explanation.surface: A dodgy dish passes off meat and eel mixed with lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat and eel confused' tempts a single anagram of both words, but only the fish is jumbled; the meat is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a colour-changing lizard, so it is a specific example of the general reptile.

clue.text: Shining passion, right? Love our team

blocks.note: lust is strong passion
R is the abbreviation for right
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O
our team is us

explanation.surface: A fan gushes about the bright passion of their beloved side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous describes something with a sheen or glow, so it matches the adjective meaning gleaming or bright.

clue.text: Powerless to protect deposit? Extremely interesting

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: powerless means unable
to deposit something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A depositor wonders whether anyone is powerless to guard their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: UN-ABLE is split after its second letter to take in the phrase for deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: A book so gripping that a reader cannot stop is called unputdownable, an informal word for something compelling.

clue.text: March broke up after time

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
broke means having no money, poor

explanation.surface: A military march fell apart after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning disbanded; here 'broke' is poor and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To troop is to walk together in a body, so as verbs the two describe the same orderly movement.

clue.text: Start broadcast outside

blocks.note: to open is to start
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A radio show is about to begin transmitting from an outdoor location.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air events take place outdoors rather than under a roof, so the adjective means out of doors.

clue.text: Song from Scandinavian about climbing in south-east

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters run upwards, so they read backwards
'in' places the climbing letters inside the compass pair

blocks.note: SE is the compass abbreviation
a Dane is from Denmark, a Scandinavian country
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian mountaineer sings while climbing in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scandinavian and 'about' together are reversed, then set between S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song, traditionally sung by a lover beneath a window, so it is a type of the definition.

clue.text: Attack in space seen in old-fashioned light

indicators.note: 'in' sets one word inside another

blocks.note: a gap is a space
to slam is to attack in words, to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A sci-fi assault in outer space appears under an antique glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas lamps lit Victorian streets before electricity, so the term names a lamp of an earlier era.

clue.text: Allowable departure from fact in Celtic epic one translated

indicators.note: translating turns text into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A translator takes liberties with an ancient Celtic saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom writers are allowed to bend facts or rules for artistic effect.

clue.text: Lord going round island aboard launch

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so the lord wraps the rest

blocks.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, a lord
I is the abbreviation for island
aboard a ship is on it

explanation.surface: A nobleman sails round an island on a small motor boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' looks like the boat; it is the verb meaning to start something new.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to be first to develop it, which is to launch or initiate it.

clue.text: Stand for picture

blocks.note: first meaning: to act or speak on behalf of, or symbolise
second meaning: to depict or portray in art

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for picture' reads like posing for a portrait; the two parts are separate senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both symbolising or acting for something and depicting it in an image.

clue.text: Clear sound of aircraft

indicators.note: 'sound of' asks for a word that is spoken the same as another

blocks.note: an aircraft is a plane

explanation.surface: The roar of a jet is heard distinctly overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is obvious and easy to understand, so the adjective is a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Football club omitted radical reforms

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are put together anew

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A football club, having dropped its extremist, overhauls itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlético Madrid is a major Spanish professional side, so it is one instance of a football club.

clue.text: Born hater, unusually detestable

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so these letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who hates from birth is uncommonly loathsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means inspiring disgust and loathing, so it shares the sense of deserving hatred.

clue.text: Studious expert about plug and microphone

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the expert's word wraps the plug

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad
mic is short for microphone

explanation.surface: A bookish technician fiddles with a plug and a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests electrics next to the microphone; here it is a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic describes someone scholarly and fond of learning, so it is a close synonym of studious.

clue.text: Regiment's patron, old and single, in embrace? That is fine

indicators.note: 'in' puts the first two pieces inside the word for embrace

blocks.note: a clinch is a tight embrace
O is the abbreviation for old
lone means single, solitary
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
F is the pencil grade for fine

explanation.surface: An elderly single patron of a regiment is caught in a hug, and asks whether that is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: A British regiment's colonel-in-chief is an honorary head, often a member of the royal family; 'fine' is the pencil-grade abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The colonel-in-chief is the ceremonial head of a British regiment, usually a royal, which makes them its patron.

clue.text: Joke for example with piano during interlude

indicators.note: 'during' places something within a span, so these letters go inside the pause

blocks.note: a lull is a pause, an interlude
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
P, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A pianist cracks a gag during the interval of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word here, leaving 'example' alone to give its abbreviation; LULL opens after its first L.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a playful trick or teasing hoax, so it is an informal word for a joke at someone's expense.

clue.text: Bird above former rival

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A bird soars over its old competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rival' reads as a noun after 'former', but it is the verb; in a down clue 'above' puts the bird first.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or surpass them, which is to rival them as a verb.

clue.text: Gifts in first of seasonal dispatches

indicators.note: 'first of' asks for just the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: the opening letter of seasonal
to dispatch is to kill

explanation.surface: Christmas presents arrive in the first holiday deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatches' suggests post; it is the verb for putting to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts can mean natural talents or abilities, so a person's skills are their gifts.

clue.text: Artist and revolutionary son getting on

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
someone getting on is old, aged

explanation.surface: A painter and his radical son are both growing older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as a describing word for the son, but it turns the son plus the old word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter famous for ballet dancers, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Leave rent

blocks.note: first meaning: depart, in the slang sense of making off
second meaning: a tear or rip, as in fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like the money paid to a landlord; it is the old past tense of rend, or a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for departing quickly, and also a noun or past participle for a tear or division.

clue.text: Stirred up, be cranky, dismissing a science fiction genre

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the following letter is dropped from the mix
stirred means mixed about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be mixed, before one is dropped
the article itself, removed

explanation.surface: An irritable fan is riled about a sci-fi style he dismisses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred up' looks like one phrase, but only 'Stirred' is the signal; 'up' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberpunk is a subgenre of science fiction set in high-tech, gritty dystopian futures, so it is one kind of the genre.

clue.text: Democrat in heavy defeat almost tearful

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut
'in' places the party letter inside the rest

blocks.note: a mauling is a heavy defeat; its last letter goes
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A US Democrat facing a landslide loss is close to weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means self-pityingly sentimental and weepy, often from drink, so it is a near synonym of tearful.

clue.text: Look at you, getting into European dance

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
ye is the old form of you
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone admires a partner making their way into a continental ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The old 'you' sits between E and BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them closely, an informal verb for looking at.

clue.text: Portion covered by pretty small item of clothing

definitions.note: the answer is plural in form, like trousers, but names one garment

indicators.note: being covered by something means being enclosed, so the portion goes inside

blocks.note: cute means pretty
a lot is a portion, one's share
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A small part is hidden under a pretty little garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small item of clothing' reads as one phrase, but 'small' belongs to the wordplay and the garment is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Culottes are women's knee-length trousers cut to look like a skirt, so they are a garment.

clue.text: Tension, some assert, still around

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the following words
'around' means the run of letters is turned round, read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Some people claim tension still lingers in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain, so it is a direct synonym of tension.
